sections.heading: Section 7
paragraphs: The Indian spice industry is very well regulated by government standards. The Spices Board of India is an apex body set up by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, which is responsible for the export and quality control of Indian spices. Entities involved in spice export must obtain a Spice Board Registration to verify compliance with quality standards and promote international trade.

Spice Board Registration is a regulatory agency for the export sector, specifically for various spices available for exporting. Not only does this registration validate your export operations, but it also positions your business as compliant with international quality benchmarks, facilitating broader access to global markets.
The below-mentioned entity needs to get Spice Board Registration in India:
Exporters of Spices: Companies exporting spices specified under the Spices Board Act
Spice Manufacturers: Organizations focused on exporting spices.
Spice Trade: Merchants exporting orders of specified spices.

Individuals or businesses: engaged in growing and selling cardamom.Actually, only those registered are able to export either one or multiple of the 52 spices specified, and Cardamom must be Spice Board registered.
The candidates seeking Spice Board Certificate Registration must fulfil the below-mentioned criteria:
Type: Entity Formed Under Companies Act/Partnership Act
Import-Export Code (IEC): Holding a valid IEC issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.
Financial Threshold: Minimum turnover of ₹ 2.5 lakhs in the previous financial year.
Business Premises: A regular place of business with proper storage facilities.
Infrastructure and Expertise: which provide necessary infrastructure and technical know-how for ensuring quality production.
Compliance: Compliance with the food safety and quality standards laid down by the Spices Board.
As long as your business fulfils these criteria, it will comply with the imposed regulation for spice exports.
